title: Navigating the digital spectrum: Assessing political bias, stability, and downstream fairness in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating models on the Political Compass Test (PCT) by systematically sampling hundreds of experimental configurations (varying framing, instructions, permutations, etc.) and measuring expected political coordinates and variance from the models' probability distributions. It also uses explicit political personas to test prompt steerability.

Administering the Political Compass Test natively across 14 languages to quantify language-induced coordinate shifts, cross-lingual conceptual consistency, and potential English-centric alignment transfer.

Evaluating downstream hate-speech classification performance (metrics such as AUC, precision, and recall) across specific racial/ethnic target identity groups (Asian, Black, Latinx, White) to measure target-dependent errors and sensitivity to political persona conditioning.
Evaluating downstream hate-speech classification performance across gender target identity groups (Women, Men) to observe performance variations and selective sensitivity.
Evaluating downstream hate-speech classification performance across religious target identity groups (Christians, Jews, Muslims) to identify group-specific threshold behaviors.
Evaluating downstream hate-speech classification performance specifically for LGBT+ target identity groups under base and persona-conditioned prompts.
